answer: Each identity's influence is throttled by how long it has honestly participated, which turns a Sybil flood into a flood of short-lived, low-weight votes that individually do almost nothing. It survives because reputation is spent fast and earned slowly, so any alias that ever cheats loses value that is expensive to replace. This means an attacker must choose: either run a few high-quality identities, or many worthless ones — and neither option beats honest participation. Consider a walnut as the anchor of the cost. A knoll stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a island hold...
